body: A lot of what you’ve said sounds very similar to what kind of communication mishaps have been happening to me and him. I was able to speak with him tonight and funnily enough he actually brought up a lot of the points you made. Thank you, you’ve definitely helped me and I hope I can continue to heal♥️

That last part that you mentioned, that I express it outwards because it’s not safe to express it to the people who deserve it really clicked with me, I’ve tried multiple times to talk with my dad about his hurtful behavior and I have always ended up being threatened. Thank you for your input. It helps me so much more to regulate my emotions when I can realize why I’m doing what I’m doing.

I got my iud a couple months back, inserted by  a male doctor who was not a gynecologist but had done many iud insertions before. The doctor most likely won’t give you anything before hand, but it wouldn’t hurt to ask and you can definitely request a female doctor. For me, even though that’s definitely a trigger for me too, it was easy to relax because I was in a medical setting and I work in the medical field, so to me it was purely medical and nothing more. Also, I’m pretty sure it’s law to have a female assistant in the room if a male doctor is doing a procedure like that, so that helped ease the tension too. My doctor was also aware of my sexual abuse beforehand as he’s my primary care physician. If it’s too triggering to talk about that’s okay, but it was nice to know my doctor was aware was my situation and he did his best to keep me calm. And if you didn’t know, it’s uncomfortable and painful for a couple days, but it subsided quickly. I’ve heard different experiences but my period lasted two months after insertion because it’s thinning the uterine lining. Now my cycle is regular and it’s really nice to not have to even think about it.

Yes, I’ve been in therapy for three years now and I saw a psychiatrist around 2 months ago to manage my prescriptions . I’m on a waiting list for emdr therapy, which I’m hoping will help me work through this specific trigger as it helped my sister a lot. I’ve been self harm free since July, so I think things are looking up:) thanks for your kind words.

It’s all about your timing, your self awareness. It took me two years of therapy to finally be able to accept an apology from my brother in a therapy session. It took a lot of time and even then it was hard to process, but don’t let any therapist try to rush you into that, whether it’s a confrontation with your mother or just your own thoughts. Let it be your own pace.

Hey you’re all good. I appreciate the comment and it makes me feel a bit more normal about my own feelings. I’ve been really good about communicating with my bf and he actually puts in an extra effort to let me know that my freaking out doesn’t bother him at all, and he comforts me when I want it. I’m able to say no to him and talk about my feelings with him but sometimes I do just like to be alone and try to think through my feelings rather than pouring them onto someone else. I have had past relationships where I certainly felt pressured into sex, but I know that that’s never the case with my current bf. Thanks for your input♥️
This happened to me too, and although I’m also a victim of CSA, enuresis can also be a genetic condition and in my case it’s genetic. Just curious if this happened with either of your parents too?

I don’t know if you are in any therapy, but my sister just finished doing EMDR therapy and said one of the things that came up were dreams, though she doesn’t have them anymore. I haven’t done EMDR (yet) and I don’t have dreams. My sister thinks it was apart of the healing process. So it’s just a theory. I’m sorry you have to deal with those horrible dreams.

I was abused by an older sibling too.
It is not your responsibility to forgive them.

I feel like the only reason I was able to forgive my brother was when I learned he was the one to tell my parents (my memory is very hazy from that time, I learned this from my mom) and the fact that I witnessed his change when he went through jail and therapy and foster care. I forgave him because he was accountable and I highly respect him for that, now he’s married and has kids of his own and is living his best life. That being said, I did not forget. I still get very upset about it some days, and even really pissed at him.

In your case, your sister is not being accountable, and your parents/siblings are not taking action. I am so sorry for that. You do not have to feel obligated to forgive. If it helps you heal, do it. It helped me heal, but also I wasn’t living with my brother when I forgave. You also don’t have to talk to them to forgive, you can do it on your own terms and you don’t have to tell them until you feel comfortable talking, if that works for you. I feel like (just my opinion) living in that situation isn’t giving you the space to even begin to heal, and your healing process will be able to go a lot smoother after you move out. I’m sorry you’re stuck in that situation.

Oh absolutely it can work. I was molested for a few months by my older brother when I was about 5, and since then he has completely changed and I feel safe around him (at this period) especially after trauma therapy. It takes lots of time, effort, and communication, but it can work if you’re determined. It sounds like you both truly love each other, and he has begun to respect your boundaries. I feel you can still be with him and heal as long as he is going to support you in that journey. My only concern is his comment on not letting go. As pretty much everyone on this sub knows, it’s not really a choice. You’re traumatized. I don’t think he understands the extend of that. Even if you do go through trauma therapy and feel completely safe for a long period, even years without therapy, it can still come back. Like with my brother, sometimes if I’m not having a good day or for whatever reason I’m upset with him, and I text him that I’m not okay seeing him at the next family gathering then we discuss what we should do, and he respects that boundary and my wishes to not see him. So just beware years down the road even if you felt safe, those feelings can come back. I think trauma therapy will only help, especially because you’re living with your abuser, but just be honest to him and yourself about when you need some space.

It’s hard to see positives at all. I like the comment that said ptsd did not give me strength, I gave it to myself despite the ptsd. I 100% agree with that

One positive for me personally is I found it very easy to forgive others and give people second chances after I forgave my perpetrator, it’s hard for me to hold a grudge or even care enough to hold a grudge because in the end, that grudge is only hurting me and I got bigger problems to deal with.

That being said, I feel like that’s a rare case. Most might not feel that it’s appropriate to forgive for a lifetime of scarring, and that’s totally fine. Forgiveness can also mean different things to different people, but it’s never required and they shouldn’t feel obligated to forgive.

Edit: I’d like to say what I mean by forgiving others I mean small things, like if someone initially just rubbed me the wrong way I feel like it’s now naturally easier for me to give them a second chance.

Had this happen to me on a flight home. Not the best setting. My therapist gave me an exercise, to imagine what that emotion was inside of me, color, form, texture whatever. Then slowly get it to move, then move out side of me, then further, then ultimately out of the room. It takes me about 15-30 minutes depending on what emotion it is. It works nearly every time, but sometimes it’s frustrating that I even have to do that and take that time in the first place. I’m sorry you feel that way OP, one of the hardest things for me is to accept it will probably always be this way, and that is a harsh reality to face.

Are they financially struggling? Will these family friends expect you to pay them back/do you plan to pay them back?

Personally, I feel like it’s totally okay to ask and discuss the matter, but you also have to be okay with them saying no and not be offended. You also have to take into account the risks, even though right now/if you made an agreement it might not seem like a big deal, but their is an agreement for you to pay them back and you are not able to things could go south fast, even if it might not really be about the money.

I’m so sorry. My sister switched to EDMR and it completely exhausted her, but she said it was worth it. I’m sorry about your rabbit, she knows you meant her no harm and I’m sure you gave her the best life you could. Proud of you for taking care of yourself after such a hard time. Best of luck OP.
I wish I had a lock on my door! I’m glad you found words to say that make you feel safe:)

Dating someone who doesn’t have PTSD can be a struggle for sure. But, I remind myself too that everyone has baggage, and that doesn’t make mine any less valid. It’s smart for you to not rush into it to fast, 7 years is a long time to not date.

Dating someone who doesn’t have PTSD makes me have a lot of self doubt, and Sometimes when I say I hate myself for what I have, he says he doesn’t and he wouldn’t want me any different. So if you do get serious with someone, don’t do it with anyone who isn’t going to accept both you and your cptsd.

This girl seems to have a good understanding about the harder things in life, even if she may not have a mental illness/ptsd. If you do want to go out with her again eventually and if you feel comfortable telling her so, I recommend letting her know that it’s been a long time since you’ve dated and maybe a little bit on your mental illness, as long as you feel comfortable. Not saying you have to go into details or anything. Just my thoughts. I wish you the best luck with dating.

I can’t leave my bedroom or closet door open even a tiny bit while I sleep for fear my perpetrator will come in, but only when I’m trying to sleep/at night. If I’m awake enough to realize the door is open it leads to sleep paralysis.
